references.text: Joshua is appointed before Eleazar the priest, as Moses was commanded to do.
Moses receives a command to strengthen and encourage Joshua, who will lead the people into the land.
Joshua receives his command and mission before the entire assembly.
Joshua takes over leadership after Moses' death and receives the Lord's command to be strong and courageous.
The fulfillment of this command where Moses presents Joshua before Eleazar and lays hands on him.
Aaron and his sons were presented at the entrance to the tent sanctuary, a pattern for public appointment.
The seven were presented before the apostles who laid hands on them, a parallel to public appointment for service.
Paul urges Timothy not to be too quick to lay hands on anyone, referring to public appointment.
